native_input.per_format_sequence: five forward, two reverse, short rebound

interpretation: On this iPhone, the mesh path has a steadier raster tail while spending more time on the UI thread. Both paths use GPU rasterization; no default renderer changed.
limitations: Single device and short warm runs; no soak or 120 Hz validation.
No Apple Books visual parity claim; mesh and shader are not pixel-equivalent.
FrameTiming raster wall time is not isolated GPU kernel time; budget exceedance is not actual dropped-frame rate.
UIKit event timestamps and FrameTiming have different origins; event-to-raster samples are rejected.
Dart dispatch-to-raster excludes system input queue before Dart, presentation and display scanout.
RGBA cache accounting excludes native/PDF/transient GPU allocations; RSS is whole-process memory.
Functional integration-test cancellation does not prove native OS interruption handling.
Source books, screenshots, device identifiers, signing metadata and private paths are excluded.

mesh_native_comparison.delivery: Same XCTest UIKit drag sequence; separate app builds/runs, not paired trials or same-process input comparison.
mesh_native_comparison.observed_outlier: First mesh EPUB drag had 113.631 ms dispatch-to-raster; retained, not removed from percentiles. Cause unproven; startup/pipeline warmup is a hypothesis.
mesh_native_comparison.interpretation: Mesh improves observed P95; median is similar. This does not establish end-to-end touch latency or universal superiority.
